USMLE-style practice · Pediatrics

Routine treatment of a stable infant

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 7-month-old with typical bronchiolitis has oxygen saturation of 95% on room air, mild recession and adequate hydration. A parent asks for an inhaler because a sibling has asthma. Which management plan is best?

  1. Supportive care and monitoring without routine salbutamol
  2. Scheduled inhaled salbutamol throughout the illness
  3. A short course of oral prednisolone
  4. Nebulized epinephrine followed by a home bronchodilator
  5. Oral amoxicillin while awaiting a viral test
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Supportive care and monitoring without routine salbutamol

Routine bronchodilators do not improve typical bronchiolitis outcomes; care focuses on breathing and hydration.

Understanding the options

Supportive care and monitoring without routine salbutamol
Routine bronchodilators do not improve typical bronchiolitis outcomes; care focuses on breathing and hydration.
Scheduled inhaled salbutamol throughout the illness
Routine salbutamol has no established role in typical infant bronchiolitis.
A short course of oral prednisolone
Routine corticosteroids are not recommended for typical bronchiolitis.
Nebulized epinephrine followed by a home bronchodilator
This is not routine bronchiolitis therapy; epinephrine has a different role in croup.
Oral amoxicillin while awaiting a viral test
No bacterial features are given, and a viral test is not needed to justify supportive care in a typical case.
